attrs.text: **Windows extra roots** — Additional directory grants apply to the harness `write` and `edit` tools only. PowerShell, terminals, PTC, and other sandboxed processes retain workspace and private-temp access under `workspace-write`. Extra grants do not change their ACLs or block their execution; see the [decision](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-10-29-windows-file-tool-directory-grants.md).

title: **Windows ACL enforcement is partial** — NTFS hard links alias one file object across workspace and external paths, reads stay unconfined, and a tree another AppContainer tool has ACL'd with a package SID is unreadable to the Low-integrity ...

attrs.text: **Windows ACL enforcement is partial** — NTFS hard links alias one file object across workspace and external paths, reads stay unconfined, and a tree another AppContainer tool has ACL'd with a package SID is unreadable to the Low-integrity child. The provider reports `enforcement: 'partial'` rather than overstating that boundary as full.

title: **Diagnosis preserves integrity labels** — it cannot fix Low-labeled executables affecting programs launched outside DSH. It also cannot repair a caller's missing `WRITE_DAC`; extracted and recovery scripts are user-writable and are not sup...

attrs.text: **Diagnosis preserves integrity labels** — it cannot fix Low-labeled executables affecting programs launched outside DSH. It also cannot repair a caller's missing `WRITE_DAC`; extracted and recovery scripts are user-writable and are not supported elevated entrypoints. Resource directories can remain after an unclean shutdown.

title: **Wide-directory and FAT-volume warnings are deferred; the FAT-class residue is unverified** — the UI-side warnings are not implemented, a FAT volume as a grant root fails loudly, and a FAT-class target outside the granted roots stores no s...

attrs.text: **Wide-directory and FAT-volume warnings are deferred; the FAT-class residue is unverified** — the UI-side warnings are not implemented, a FAT volume as a grant root fails loudly, and a FAT-class target outside the granted roots stores no security descriptor; its effective integrity label is assigned by the system rather than recorded on the object, so the label layer's behavior there is untested. FAT stays legacy residue.

title: **The bundled diagnosis skill needs an unconfined caller** — both the classification and the repairs read or write security descriptors a confined child cannot reach, so the session must escalate that one call; with no approval channel the ...

attrs.text: **The bundled diagnosis skill needs an unconfined caller** — both the classification and the repairs read or write security descriptors a confined child cannot reach, so the session must escalate that one call; with no approval channel the escalation fails closed and the path stays undiagnosed.

title: **PowerShell language mode differs by confined mode** — under `read-only`, PowerShell cannot create its AppLocker probe files in temp and conservatively starts in ConstrainedLanguage (`Add-Type`, non-core .NET static calls, COM, and reflect...

attrs.text: **PowerShell language mode differs by confined mode** — under `read-only`, PowerShell cannot create its AppLocker probe files in temp and conservatively starts in ConstrainedLanguage (`Add-Type`, non-core .NET static calls, COM, and reflection fail); the shipped `workspace-write` path lets the probe complete, so pwsh stays in FullLanguage unless host-wide WDAC/AppLocker policy says otherwise, while a direct `AclSandbox` with `tempDir: null` has no such guarantee. This split is PowerShell startup behavior, not part of the ACL write boundary.

title: **One write allowlist per workspace** — the write SID is the unit of the allowlist and IS the workspace identity; reusing one sandbox instance across two workspaces widens both grants to both roots. Create one instance per workspace root — ...

attrs.text: **One write allowlist per workspace** — the write SID is the unit of the allowlist and IS the workspace identity; reusing one sandbox instance across two workspaces widens both grants to both roots. Create one instance per workspace root — the seam does exactly this, keyed by the workspace path.

title: **Cleanup is best-effort by design** — `dispose()` attempts every temp revocation and aggregates failures into an `AggregateError`; a cleanup failure can leave the random directory and its temp-SID-only ACE behind. Once the process exits no...

attrs.text: **Cleanup is best-effort by design** — `dispose()` attempts every temp revocation and aggregates failures into an `AggregateError`; a cleanup failure can leave the random directory and its temp-SID-only ACE behind. Once the process exits no future token carries that SID, so the residue is inert until OS temp hygiene or manual removal reclaims it.

title: **Standing workspace ACEs are invisible residue** — renaming a workspace derives a new SID; the old ACEs on the old path stay (inert, write-SID-only), and a future cleanup command may reap them.

attrs.text: **Standing workspace ACEs are invisible residue** — renaming a workspace derives a new SID; the old ACEs on the old path stay (inert, write-SID-only), and a future cleanup command may reap them.

title: **NULL-DACL directories are not identity-preserving under grant+revoke** — a directory with a NULL DACL means "everyone full control"; `grantWrite` builds the new ACL from that null, and the revoke round-trip leaves an empty (deny-all) DACL...

attrs.text: **NULL-DACL directories are not identity-preserving under grant+revoke** — a directory with a NULL DACL means "everyone full control"; `grantWrite` builds the new ACL from that null, and the revoke round-trip leaves an empty (deny-all) DACL rather than the original NULL DACL. Real workspace and temp directories carry real DACLs, so this stays a documented edge.

title: **Piped stdio capture is impossible for confined grandchildren** — libuv's pipe stdio uses named pipes, whose client-end open requests write access no restricting SID is granted (the Win32 layer's default SD template, not the token default ...

attrs.text: **Piped stdio capture is impossible for confined grandchildren** — libuv's pipe stdio uses named pipes, whose client-end open requests write access no restricting SID is granted (the Win32 layer's default SD template, not the token default DACL), so `spawn(..., { stdio: 'pipe' })` inside a confined process fails with EPERM; inherited and ignored stdio spawns work, and anonymous pipes (PowerShell pipelines) work because the restricted token's default DACL carries a full-access restricting-SID ACE.

title: **Grant materialization is an eager full-tree propagation** — `SetNamedSecurityInfoW` on a directory with inheritable ACEs walks every descendant immediately (tens of seconds on large workspace trees); the per-workspace identity pays it onc...

attrs.text: **Grant materialization is an eager full-tree propagation** — `SetNamedSecurityInfoW` on a directory with inheritable ACEs walks every descendant immediately (tens of seconds on large workspace trees); the per-workspace identity pays it once per workspace per machine, and the exact-ACE skip makes every later provision cheap.

title: **Read-side confinement and network policy are out of scope** — `WRITE_RESTRICTED` intersects write accesses only; pair this backend with a read-side policy for stronger confinement.

attrs.text: **Read-side confinement and network policy are out of scope** — `WRITE_RESTRICTED` intersects write accesses only; pair this backend with a read-side policy for stronger confinement.

title: **Reads stop at objects another AppContainer-based tool has ACL'd with a package SID** — a file whose DACL carries an ACE for a package SID (`S-1-15-2-…`) is inaccessible to a Low-integrity token on this host, even when the same DACL grants...

attrs.text: **Reads stop at objects another AppContainer-based tool has ACL'd with a package SID** — a file whose DACL carries an ACE for a package SID (`S-1-15-2-…`) is inaccessible to a Low-integrity token on this host, even when the same DACL grants the user full control and Everyone read (observed: adding that single ACE to a fresh file reproduces the denial, granting Everyone read does not lift it, and the same bytes copied elsewhere stay readable). The kernel rule behind it is unconfirmed and not this package's to change; tools that sandbox themselves with AppContainers stamp such ACEs, so a tree they touched becomes unreadable to this backend's child. Removing the foreign ACE (or re-installing the affected tree) restores access.

title: **File effects are the whole policy vocabulary** — the seam expresses no network, process, syscall, device, or credential restrictions.

attrs.text: **File effects are the whole policy vocabulary** — the seam expresses no network, process, syscall, device, or credential restrictions.

title: **Runner diagnostics are in-band** — exit status plus stderr evidence cannot prove which process wrote a matching line, so a confined child that deliberately mimics its runner can cause a false availability or diagnostic attribution; this c...

attrs.text: **Runner diagnostics are in-band** — exit status plus stderr evidence cannot prove which process wrote a matching line, so a confined child that deliberately mimics its runner can cause a false availability or diagnostic attribution; this cannot bypass confinement, and an out-of-band runner-status channel is deferred.
